body:
I can confirm @BastiaanOlij's approach works: Mobile (this PR) | Mobile (this PR, HDR 2D) | Mobile (Bastiaan's approach) | Mobile (Bastiaan's approach, HDR 2D) -|-|-|- | | | Forward+ for comparison: **Testing project:** [test_blend_modes.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33484245/test_blend_modes.zip)
Diff (also contains the GLSL define) ```diff diff --git a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp index ff40bb5eab9..ab28e169066 100644 --- a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp +++ b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/scene_shader_forward_mobile.cpp @@ -844,6 +844,7 @@ void SceneShaderForwardMobile::init(const String p_defines) { actions.render_mode_defines["debug_shadow_splits"] = "#define DEBUG_DRAW_PSSM_SPLITS\n"; actions.render_mode_defines["fog_disabled"] = "#define FOG_DISABLED\n"; + actions.render_mode_defines["blend_mul"] = "#define BLEND_MUL\n"; actions.render_mode_defines["specular_occlusion_disabled"] = "#define SPECULAR_OCCLUSION_DISABLED\n"; diff --git a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl index d05ae23fac6..24ac34c10a7 100644 --- a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl +++ b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl @@ -2421,9 +2421,15 @@ void main() { out_color.rgb = mix(out_color.rgb, fog.rgb, fog.a); #endif // !FOG_DISABLED - // On mobile we use a UNORM buffer with 10bpp which results in a range from 0.0 - 1.0 resulting in HDR breaking - // We divide by sc_luminance_multiplier to support a range from 0.0 - 2.0 both increasing precision on bright and darker images +#ifdef BLEND_MUL + out_color.rgb = out_color.rgb; +#else + // On mobile, we use a UNORM buffer with 10bpp which results in a range from 0.0 - 1.0 resulting in HDR breaking. + // We divide by sc_luminance_multiplier to support a range from 0.0 - 2.0, both increasing precision on bright and darker images. + // This should not be done when using the Multiply blend mode to prevent it from looking too dark. out_color.rgb = out_color.rgb / sc_luminance_multiplier(); +#endif + #ifdef PREMUL_ALPHA_USED out_color.rgb *= premul_alpha; #endif ```
